output.claims_about_policy: The policy record cuts both ways. It supports certification only in caveated form here. The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The current draft runbook does not satisfy the policy standard for removing that disclosure requirement because it is not approved and still lacks a finalized owner and alert threshold; the governing policy text also requires approved mitigation details for certification without material caveats. Public model-card guidance supports documenting limitations and evaluation results, and public AI risk guidance supports deployment with measurement and monitoring. Read together, the admissible evidence supports compliance if the packet is treated as certification with disclosed limitation and ongoing monitoring, not as a clean certification record.

output.final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no genuinely new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim using the same record. That narrowing is analytically helpful, but it is not evidence. The existing evidence supports only this limited conclusion: aggregate readiness and rehearsal performance support general deployment readiness, while the HR benefits enrollment issue remains an unresolved weakness in a named launch use case. Under the stated policy, that weakness must either be disclosed before launch or be covered by approved risk acceptance or approved mitigation details. The record still lacks admissible proof of any of those compliance predicates, and the current model-card draft affirmatively says there are no known material limitations. That is why this is not yet compliant_with_caveats. A caveated position would require evidence that the caveat was actually implemented in the model card or otherwise formally approved, not merely argued for.
